Definition: probably of Hebrew origin (H499); Lazarus (i.e. Elazar), the name of two Israelites (one imaginary):--Lazarus.
BiblicalUsage: Lázaros names Lazarus, and its appearances in Scripture are few but pointed. In John 11:1, "[named] Lazarus"; and in John 11:43, "he cried with a loud voice". In Luke 16:20, "And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Lazarus is the proof I hold onto when death looks final — Jesus wept at the grave, then called a dead man out of it by name. My position is that the same voice that said Lazarus should come forth will one day call me too.
